newsitem.title: THAILAND: Minister wants to keep Thai oil reserve at 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Minister wants to keep Thai oil reserve at 5 pct.

text.p: Thai Commerce Minister Chucheep Harnsawat said on Wednesday that reserves of imported oil products should be kept at five percent of annual imports and not 10 percent as required by the government from next January.
He told reporters that the board of the National Energy Policy Office, of which he is a member, would meet on Thursday to discuss the national oil reserve policy.
"The five percent reserve (for imported products) is reasonable. If the reserve is increased, the cost of building storage and other expenses would be eventually passed on to consumers," he said.

Importers of refined oil products into Thailand are to be required to double their stockpiles to 10 percent from January 1997. The plan is part of an effort to raise reserves following the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.

In an effort to ensure sufficient reserves, Thailand initially raised the requirement to five percent from three percent of annual oil supply, with a goal to eventually increase it to 10 percent for imported refined products.

The increase was also aimed at reducing the advantage importers currently have over local producers who are at present required to reserve five percent of their crude imports and five percent of oil products.
